subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which session identity and token semantics should the user-facing overflow diagnostic expose across private and shared channel surfaces?
rationale: The implementation can be bounded, but raw session keys may reveal channel or infrastructure identifiers and available token totals may be estimated, provider-observed, or stale; code cannot safely choose the disclosure and wording policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Safe structured diagnostics
options.body: Show a redacted display label, provider/model, effective budget, and explicitly distinguish observed from estimated token counts while omitting raw IDs and paths.

options.title: Numeric details only
options.body: Show provider/model, budget, count provenance, and recovery actions but omit all session identity from the user-visible message.

options.title: Keep generic guidance
options.body: Retain the existing recovery message and leave detailed session and budget evidence in logs and status surfaces only.

recommendation.title: Safe structured diagnostics
recommendation.body: Show a redacted display label, provider/model, effective budget, and explicitly distinguish observed from estimated token counts while omitting raw IDs and paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history spans the runner, recovery, and auto-reply surfaces where a consistent disclosure policy must be applied.
